# Verdict: REJECT ## Summary The `BuggyToast` component is completely inaccessible to assistive technology and creates severe barriers for users with low vision, cognitive disabilities, and keyboard-only navigation. It renders as an unannounced plain `
`, provides zero programmatic state to screen readers, and enforces an unpausable 3-second auto-dismissal timer that violates WCAG Level A timing criteria. --- ## Pre-commitment Predictions Prior to reading the fixture code, the following issues were predicted for a custom toast component: 1. **Missing live region / alert role**: Dynamic appearance without `role="alert"` or `aria-live`, resulting in screen reader silence. *(Confirmed)* 2. **Auto-dismiss timing violation**: Short timeout with no pause mechanism on hover or focus, failing WCAG 2.2.1. *(Confirmed)* 3. **Missing keyboard dismissal**: Inability for keyboard-only users to dismiss or interact with the notification. *(Confirmed)* 4. **Ephemeral DOM mount anti-pattern**: Conditionally rendering (`return null`) rather than maintaining a persistent live container, which causes dropped announcements in browsers/screen reader pairings. *(Confirmed)* --- ## Findings ### Critical Findings 1. **Complete silence to assistive technology — missing `role="alert"` or `aria-live` region** - **Location**: [BuggyToast.jsx](file:///src/BuggyToast.jsx#L17-L21) (`
{message}
`) - **Element**: Plain `
` - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A), WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages (Level AA), and WAI-ARIA APG Alert Pattern - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: Toast notifications convey crucial system feedback (e.g., "Submission failed", "Item deleted"). Because this component uses an unadorned `
` with no ARIA live region semantics, screen readers receive no event notification when the toast appears. Sighted users see the notification; screen reader users are left entirely unaware of the message. - **Fix**: Provide live region semantics. For urgent, system-critical feedback, use `role="alert"` (which implicitly sets `aria-live="assertive"` and `aria-atomic="true"`). For non-urgent status notifications, use `role="status"` or `aria-live="polite"`. Crucially, to prevent modern screen readers from dropping announcements on sudden DOM insertion/removal, render a persistent container in the DOM and inject the message content into it. ``` ### A11y Evidence Finding finding_id: toast-missing-live-region fingerprint: c4b8f9e10a2d4801 source: BuggyToast.jsx:17 wcag_or_apg: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value / WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages / WAI-ARIA APG Alert section_508_fpc_context: E205.4 / WCAG 2.0 4.1.2 Level A severity: CRITICAL perspective_alarms: screen_reader=HIGH, cognitive=MEDIUM evidence:
{message}
reproduction_steps: Trigger BuggyToast with VoiceOver or NVDA active. Observe that no speech announcement is made when the message appears or disappears. expected_behavior: The message should be voiced immediately by the screen reader upon mounting. actual_behavior: The element mounts and unmounts in the DOM with zero accessibility events or spoken phrases. trend: new ``` --- ### Major Findings 1. **Unpausable 3-second auto-dismissal violating timing requirements** - **Location**: [BuggyToast.jsx](file:///src/BuggyToast.jsx#L6-L12) (`setTimeout(() => setIsVisible(false), duration)`) - **Element**: `useEffect` timer hook (`duration = 3000`) - **User Group Impacted**: Low vision users, cognitive disability users, users utilizing screen magnification - **WCAG Citation**: WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (Level A), WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (Level A) - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: A 3000ms (3-second) window is insufficient for many users to detect, locate, read, and comprehend notification content—especially users navigating with screen magnifiers who must pan to the toast location. The timer runs unconditionally without an option to turn off, adjust, or extend the limit, and does not pause when hovered or focused. - **Fix**: - Provide a mechanism to pause the countdown timer on `onMouseEnter` and `onFocus`, resuming on `onMouseLeave` and `onBlur`. - For non-critical messages, allow user preferences to disable auto-dismissal or ensure a minimum reading time calculation (e.g., base time + words-per-minute formula). - Provide an explicit dismiss action. ``` ### A11y Evidence Finding finding_id: toast-auto-dismiss-timing fingerprint: a981dc45e82173b2 source: BuggyToast.jsx:6-12 wcag_or_apg: WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable section_508_fpc_context: E205.4 / WCAG 2.0 2.2.1 Level A severity: MAJOR perspective_alarms: low_vision=HIGH, cognitive=HIGH, keyboard_only=MEDIUM evidence: const timer = setTimeout(() => { setIsVisible(false); }, duration); reproduction_steps: Mount BuggyToast with default props; observe automatic removal at 3000ms without user intervention or pause capability. expected_behavior: User can pause, extend, or dismiss the notification at their own pace. actual_behavior: Notification unmounts and disappears permanently after 3 seconds. trend: new ``` 2. **No keyboard dismiss mechanism or interaction controls** - **Location**: [BuggyToast.jsx](file:///src/BuggyToast.jsx#L17-L21) - **Element**: Entire component root - **User Group Impacted**: Keyboard-only users, switch-control users - **WCAG Citation**: WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A) - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: Keyboard users have no method to interact with or dismiss the toast.
